questions.stem: Which of the following describes the charge of particles composing cathode rays?

options.D: A mixture of positively and negatively charged particles

Which of the following compounds is generally considered a weak electrolyte in aqueous solution?

options.C: Decrease in temperature and increase in pressure

options.A: Sodium at anode and chlorine at cathode
options.B: Sodium at cathode and oxygen at anode
options.C: Sodium at cathode and chlorine at anode
options.D: Hydrogen at cathode and chlorine at anode

questions.stem: What does Faraday's First Law of Electrolysis state about the mass of a liberated substance?

options.A: It is proportional to the square of the current.
options.B: It is proportional to its molar mass.
options.C: It is proportional to the quantity of electricity passing through the electrolyte.
options.D: It is inversely proportional to the time of electrolysis.

questions.stem: Gases exhibit remarkable deviation from ideal behavior particularly at low temperatures and high pressures primarily because:

options.A: The volume occupied by gas molecules is large compared to the total volume of the gas.
options.B: Molecules do not exert any force of attraction on each other.
options.C: Molecules do exert forces of attraction on each other and their volume is non-negligible.

Stoichiometry is NOT typically used for which of the following purposes?

options.A: Predicting the quantities of species required to produce products
options.B: Estimating the number of molecules involved in chemical reactions
options.C: Choosing the most economical route to products formation in industry
options.D: Determining the rate and mechanism of a chemical reaction

options.A: The feasibility of a chemical reaction (\Delta G)
options.B: The speed of a chemical reaction
options.C: The orderliness of a chemical reaction (\Delta S)
options.D: The enthalpy of a chemical reaction (\Delta H)

Which of these is NOT a characteristic of the order of a chemical reaction?

options.C: It can have values of whole number, fraction, or zero.

questions.stem: Following the linearization of the Arrhenius equation (\ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_{a}}{RT}), the slope of the plot of \ln k versus \frac{1}{T} is equal to:
For a first-order reaction, the half-life (t_{1/2}) is related to the rate constant (k) by the equation t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k}. If t_{1/2} = 0.6 minutes, what is the rate constant in s^{-1}?
Which statement about chemical bonding is FALSE?

options.A: The objective of chemical bonding is for each ion to attain the octet configuration.
options.B: Bonding is the strong or weak chemical attraction between two atoms.
options.C: The electrons involved in chemical combinations are located only in the outermost shell.
options.D: Bonding in electrolytes is typically ionic.

questions.stem: In electrovalent bonding, the final electronic configuration of the ions often results in the noble gas structure. Which process is NOT a way to achieve this noble gas structure for a non-metal atom?

options.A: Gaining electrons to the outermost shell to form the octet configuration.
options.B: Losing electrons to the outermost shell to form the octet configuration.
options.C: Non-metal atoms gain electrons to attain a noble gas structure.
options.D: Atoms can lose or gain electrons to have the noble gas structure.

questions.stem: Which of these common noble gas structures is INCORRECTLY indicated for the given ion?
Cations violating the octet rule can have various electron counts. Which electron configuration in the outermost shell is characteristic of ions that satisfy the octet rule?

options.C: 9 to 17 electrons in their outermost shells (Transition metals)

questions.stem: Which statement is FALSE regarding the nature of an electrovalent (ionic) bond?

options.A: A bond is formed by the complete transfer of one or more electrons from one atom to another.
options.B: Compounds formed are solids with high melting and boiling points.
options.C: The ions involved are held together by the Coulomb's force.
options.D: A bond is formed by the sharing of one or more electrons between atoms.

questions.stem: Which statement about covalency is FALSE?

options.A: Covalent bonding involves the sharing of electrons between two elements.
options.B: Non-metallic atoms can form covalent bonds.
options.C: The difference in electronegativity values must be less than 1.7.
options.D: The greater the difference in electronegativity, the higher the tendency to form electrovalent compounds.

questions.stem: The difference in bonding type between $AlF_{3}$ (electrovalent) and $AlCl_{3}$ (covalent) is primarily attributed to:

options.A: The fewer atoms in $AlF_{3}$ compared to $AlCl_{3}$
options.B: The larger size and lower electronegativity of Cl compared to F
options.C: The small ionic size of F coupled with its high electronegativity, contributing to a higher lattice energy of $AlF_{3}$
options.D: The higher valency of Aluminum in $AlCl_{3}$

questions.stem: Which statement concerning sigma (\sigma) and pi (\pi) bonds is FALSE?

options.A: Sigma bonds are stronger than pi bonds.
options.B: Pi bonds are formed through side-by-side overlap of atomic orbitals.
options.C: Sigma bonds are formed through head-to-head overlap of atomic orbitals.
options.D: Pi bonds are formed though head-to-head overlap of atomic orbitals.

questions.stem: Using the concept of Coulomb's law (F \propto \frac{q_{1}q_{2}}{r^{2}}), arrange the following alkali halides (NaI, NaCl, NaF, NaBr) in order of increasing ionic character.
How many sigma (\sigma) and pi (\pi) bonds are present in a diatomic nitrogen molecule ($N_{2}$)?

options.A: One sigma bond and two pi bonds
options.B: One sigma bond and one pi bond
options.C: Two sigma bonds and one pi bond
options.D: Two sigma bonds and two pi bonds
